chapter_mission: Carry the survey mission from intuition into evidence. Two worlds show the same unknown marks, and Ben's private sense of wrongness starts becoming a track he can follow.
chapter_turn: The disturbance stops being something only Ben feels and becomes something the ship can chart. Ben starts withholding in small, deliberate ways.

scene_plan.purpose: Use hyperspace routine and instrument drift to show Ben and Desh as an established team before the first world appears.
At the first world, give Ben one physical spike of wrongness and let him choose to leave it out of the report.
At the second world, repeat the marks, let Desh draw the line, and end with the survey becoming pursuit.

relationship_turns.from: operational partnership — survey team, Ch1 baseline
relationship_turns.to: co-investigators — Desh's instruments validate what Ben's Force-sense has been telling him; the partnership shifts from favor-to-a-friend toward shared reading of the same problem

relationship_turns.from: private alliance — Luke entrusted the investigation
relationship_turns.to: first withholding — Ben files the report and leaves the Force impression out. The withholding is small enough that neither father nor son would name it

exit_vector: The Steady Returns in hyperspace, pointed at uncharted coordinates. The wrongness, now anchored to a bearing, has teeth. Ben closes the chapter knowing the survey route was the corridor he was already following.
notes: Keep the chapter quiet and procedural. Ben and Desh should feel like two professionals who already know how not to talk about old damage, and the omission in the report should land as a small action rather than a confession.
